# Results — Study 843 (Waffle House Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
FEMA's informal **Waffle House Index** reads a disaster's severity off whether the
always-open chain closes; turned around into a market question: does a **major US
natural disaster** move the obvious equities — **property & casualty insurers**
(ALL/TRV/PGR) should *dip* on the payout shock, **home-improvement / rebuild** names
(HD/LOW) should *rally* on reconstruction demand? Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`06c89e09c7e9` (SPY) — also `3eba4d87a095` (ALL) / `1d9d0f43fbd0` (TRV) /
`9730d67197d9` (PGR) / `60093d13105c` (HD) / `73373520bb2e` (LOW).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), 5,555 rows each, **2004-06-01 → 2026-06-30**: SPY (benchmark), ALL/TRV/PGR (P&C insurers), HD/LOW (home-improvement). All six trade continuously across the event calendar — no survivorship holes on this window |
| Disaster table | **hardcoded** table of **16 major US-landfalling hurricanes** 2005-08-29 → 2024-10-09 (Katrina, Rita, Wilma, Ike, Sandy, Matthew, Harvey, Irma, Florence, Michael, Laura, Ida, Ian, Idalia, Helene, Milton). Landfall dates are NHC/NOAA public record; each snapped to the first NYSE session on/after landfall |
| Abnormal return | **market-adjusted** (beta-1): a name's daily return minus SPY's same-day return (Brown & Warner 1985 market-adjusted model). Baskets are equal-weight of the market-adjusted legs |
| Statistics | One-sample *t* across events (independent, far-apart calendar dates) on the per-event CAR; Newey-West HAC *t* (auto-falls-back to plain *t* at n<8); Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-calendar placebo; event-resampled bootstrap CI |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the landfall calendar date is snapped to the first NYSE session on/after it (a weekend landfall rolls to the next open). The timer enters at that session's close, exits `hold` sessions later; long-rebuilders / short-insurers, dollar-neutral; one-way cost × NAV on all **4** legs + borrow on the short leg |
| Anticipation caveat (named) | a hurricane is **forecast days before landfall**, so the market can price it in ahead of day 0 — the event window spans **[−10..+20]** and the CAR is read across the pre-storm run-up, not only the landfall session |
| Stamp window | as-of 2026-06-30 (last complete calendar month; no partial months in the stamped run) |

**Survivorship, named on the Signal axis.** ALL/TRV/PGR/HD/LOW are the *surviving*
large-cap names — this basket answers "do today's big listed insurers & rebuilders
react", not "did every P&C carrier of the era react" (a storm large enough to bankrupt
a small insurer outright is not in these five names). No survivorship trick backfills
any leg — every ticker trades the full window.

## The headline — per-event CAR over [+0..+20] sessions (market-adjusted)

| basket | mean CAR | one-sample *t* | NW *t* | direction hit rate | claim |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **Insurers** (ALL/TRV/PGR) | **+1.15%** | **+1.48** | +1.63 | down 6/16 = **37.5%** (Wilson [18.5%, 61.4%]) | claim: **dip** ❌ wrong sign |
| **Rebuilders** (HD/LOW) | **−0.28%** | **−0.25** | −0.37 | up 8/16 = **50.0%** (Wilson [28.0%, 72.0%]) | claim: **rally** ❌ wrong sign |

Both point estimates have the **wrong sign** for the folklore and neither clears the
desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar. Insurers, if anything, drift *up* ~+1.15% in the month after a
major storm (a hardening-premium / cleared-uncertainty read, not a payout dip), and the
rebuilders are flat. On direction, insurers fall on barely a third of storms and
rebuilders rally on exactly half — coin flips.

## The directional test — paired (rebuilders − insurers) CAR [+0..+20]

The folklore's single cleanest prediction: rebuilders should out-CAR insurers.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| rebuilders mean CAR | −0.28% |
| insurers mean CAR | +1.15% |
| **paired spread (reb − ins)** | **−1.43%** |
| one-sample *t* (n=16) | **−0.88** |
| Newey-West *t* | −1.06 |
| event-bootstrap 95% CI | **[−4.32%, +1.62%]** |

The spread is **negative** — the exact opposite of the prediction — and nowhere near
significant, with a CI that straddles zero by a wide margin.

## Random-calendar placebo (20 seeds × 1,000 = 20,000 draws of 16 random days)

| statistic | observed | placebo mean (sd) | two-sided *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| insurers CAR | +1.15% | +0.26% (1.03%) | **0.385** |
| rebuilders CAR | −0.28% | +0.28% (1.31%) | **0.662** |
| spread (reb − ins) | −1.43% | +0.04% (1.67%) | **0.379** |

A random calendar of 16 days reproduces every one of these numbers comfortably —
there is nothing in the tail.

## Event window — mean CAR by offset [−10..+20]

Anchored so CAR(−10) = 0. The one offset that crosses |*t*| ≥ 2 is the insurer
**daily** abnormal return at **−5 sessions** (*t* = −2.77) — a faint pre-storm dip as
the forecast firms up. With **31 offsets** tested per basket, roughly 1–2 crossing the
bar by chance is exactly expected; it has no mechanism that would make it a headline
result, does not appear in the [+0..+20] CAR test, and reverses within days. Read as a
**look-elsewhere artifact**, not a second effect.

## Robustness — the biggest storms, and sub-eras

| cut | n | insurers CAR (*t*) | rebuilders CAR (*t*) | spread (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| full sample | 16 | +1.15% (+1.48) | −0.28% (−0.25) | −1.43% (−0.88) |
| **catastrophic only** (loss-tier 3) | 7 | −0.28% (−0.36) | **+3.09% (+2.02)** | +3.36% (+1.64) |
| pre-2015 | 5 | — | — | −0.03% (−0.01) |
| 2015-onward | 11 | — | — | −2.06% (−1.00) |

The **only** nominally significant number in the whole study is the rebuilder rally in
the **7 catastrophic (tier-3) storms** — +3.09% at *t* = 2.02 (plain *t*, n=7). It is a
*post-hoc subgroup* (storms sorted by realised loss), it just barely clears the bar on
a hand-picked seven, it does **not** carry the paired spread past significance
(*t* = 1.64), and the full-sample directional result is wrong-signed and driven by the
recent era (2015+ spread −2.06%) — so it fails the desk's "robust and holds across
sub-eras" test. A grain of truth for truly catastrophic storms, not a certifiable edge.

## The timer — long rebuilders / short insurers around a disaster

Dollar-neutral, entered at the landfall-session close (calendar-known, largely
forecast — zero look-ahead), held `hold` sessions; one-way cost × NAV on all 4 legs +
50 bps/yr borrow on the short insurer leg.

| hold | gross | net (5 bps) | *t* (net) | win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 days | −57.8 bps | −78.8 bps | −0.82 | 38% |
| 10 days | −22.2 bps | −44.2 bps | −0.41 | 44% |
| 20 days | −153.3 bps | −177.2 bps | −1.22 | 25% |

The trade the folklore implies **loses money at every horizon**, gross and net — it is
short the leg (insurers) that actually drifts up and long the leg (rebuilders) that
goes nowhere. There is no edge to charge costs against.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic world: an SPY-like market + 5 single names + a TUNABLE planted
market-adjusted drift (insurers −`edge`/day, rebuilders +`edge`/day) decaying over 15
sessions; no network.

| world | directional (reb − ins) *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.12** (sd 1.19), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = +0.15%/day (seed 843) | **+3.42** (insurers *t* = −2.64, rebuilders *t* = +1.81) |

The detector is centered at zero on the null (the 2/20 crossings are the ~5% nominal
two-sided false-positive rate at n=16, not a bias) and lights up sharply on a planted
drift. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** In the [+0..+20]-session window after 16 major US hurricanes,
  insurers drift **+1.15%** (*t* = +1.48) and rebuilders **−0.28%** (*t* = −0.25) —
  **both the wrong sign** for the folklore, neither significant — and the paired
  spread is **−1.43%** (*t* = −0.88), the opposite of the prediction. The random-calendar
  placebo reproduces all of it (*p* = 0.38–0.66). The lone nominally significant cut
  (tier-3 rebuilder rally, *t* = 2.02 on n = 7) is a post-hoc subgroup that fails the
  sub-era robustness bar.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-rebuilders / short-insurers trade loses at every
  horizon (5/10/20 days), gross and net (−44 to −177 bps), win rate ≤ 44%. There is no
  edge to deploy.
- **"Does the market read the Waffle House Index?" — BUSTED.** On the modern tradable
  tape the market has already priced the storm (hurricanes are forecast days ahead), the
  post-landfall reaction is if anything backwards, and 16 events is low power — a real,
  smaller, more localized effect (a single hard-hit regional insurer, or a
  homebuilder rather than a big-box retailer) cannot be ruled out at this size, but the
  obvious ALL/TRV/PGR-dip / HD/LOW-rally story does not survive.
